articles.title: Investigations could hound Trump into retirement at Mar-a-Lago
articles.description: President Donald Trump is facing a new problem now that his Republican Party suffered major setbacks during the 2026 midterm elections: Democrats may launch investigations which trail him even after his second term is over. "The Trump administration has already pledged to fight requests for information, even launching its own threats to prosecute members of Congress for mounting unwarranted investigations, despite legal immunity lawmakers have under the Constitution," NBC News reported on Wednesday. “I expect this administration to throw any argument they can think of in the way of these requests,” Emily Berman, an expert on executive power at the University of Houston Law Center, told the network. “If you delay enough, people move on to the next outrage." NBC News noted, "Once Trump leaves office, a new president and whichever party controls Congress has to decide whether to continue to focus on a past administration’s alleged wrongdoings." Yet on the last occasion when they had the opportunity to do so, their efforts fellow short. They failed to convict Trump for his Jan. 6th coup attempt before his second election victory and the Supreme Court granted Trump immunity for many of his actions. "But the committee was able to issue a damning report that pinned the blame for Jan. 6 on Trump," NBC News added. "Two Trump allies, Steve Bannon and trade adviser Peter Navarro, were also both successfully prosecuted for contempt of Congress for refusing to comply with subpoenas issued by the Jan. 6 committee. Both served prison time." On the other hand, The Hill contributor Bill Press argued last year that the Biden administration and Democrats failed to stop future abuses of power by refusing to do enough to hold Trump and his administration accountable after his first term. "With all the problems under this second Trump administration — the economy teetering on collapse, military forces deployed in American cities, the Justice Department preying on Trump’s enemies, America waging a questionably illegal war against alleged drug smugglers from Venezuela, presidential pardons flowing from the White House, Congress surrendering its independence to the executive branch, and American politics hopelessly and bitterly divided — these are also 'times that try men’s souls,'" Press wrote in 2025. Referring to the book "Injustice: How Politics and Fear Vanquished America’s Justice Department," Washington Post investigative reporters Carol Leonnig and Aaron C. Davis argued according to Press that "it was right then, immediately after Jan. 6, that Garland had a 'fleeting moment' to hold Trump accountable. He failed to do so."
